text.tspan: The secret is typed into a page served by the MCP server itself and POSTed straight to it. The MCP client only learns that the user agreed (accept).
one process. HTTP mode: same port as /mcp (3457). stdio mode: own FLOW_PORT listener (3458).
straight to the server, not via the MCP client
Yellow bar: finishBrowserFlow() waits up to
with progress heartbeats if requested; timeout
Why URL mode: data typed in the browser (token, password, OAuth sign-in, payment) goes to the
server in step 10 and never passes through the MCP client or the model. The spec requires URL mode
for such data and requires the client to show the full URL and ask before opening it (step 4). Flow URLs
are bearer capabilities (random UUIDv4, 1 h TTL); a production server must also bind the flow to the
accept is not "finished". accept (step 6) only means the user agreed to open the URL, so it can arrive
before the page is submitted; Open WebUI sends it the moment the link is clicked. The server keeps
the call open (yellow bar) until step 11; if accept comes after the page was submitted, the wait ends at
once. On 2025-era connections elicit_url goes through the SDK shim (elicitation/create, no step 12);
elicit_url_legacy_push uses the push API and sends step 12.
